findings.issue_text: public/app/plugins/datasource/loki/querySplitting.ts:299 — P3 advisory, confidence 100: `.map((query) => datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters))` duplicates the normalization already performed at shardQuerySplitting.ts:52 whenever shardQuerySplitting.ts:163 delegates each shard group to `runSplitQuery`, so one target traversing four shard groups executes template/filter preparation five times and preparation work grows with shard fan-out; the strongest counterargument is that both public entry points need to accept raw queries, but that does not require reprocessing the already-prepared targets passed between them, so extract a prepared-query splitting helper, retain normalization at the raw entry points, and delete the repeated execution of line 299 on the shard-to-time-split path.

public/app/plugins/datasource/loki/querySplitting.ts:298 — P3, confidence 100: the verbatim sequence `.filter((query) => query.expr)` followed by `.map((query) => datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters))` (also `public/app/plugins/datasource/loki/shardQuerySplitting.ts:50-52`) filters the raw expression before interpolation, so when a nonempty variable-only expression such as `$selector` resolves to `''` it survives selection and an empty query is sent to Loki instead of being omitted, producing a backend parse error and failing the panel, while the added tests cover only nonempty substitutions and therefore miss this acceptance case.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/plugins/datasource/loki/querySplitting.ts:299 — P3 advisory, confidence 100: `.map((query) => datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters))` duplicates the normalization already performed at shardQuerySplitting.ts:52 whenever shardQuerySplitting.ts:163 delegates each shard group to `runSplitQuery`, so one target traversing four shard groups executes template/filter preparation five times and preparation work grows with shard fan-out; the strongest counterargument is that both public entry points need to accept raw queries, but that does not require reprocessing the already-prepared targets passed between them, so extract a prepared-query splitting helper, retain normalization at the raw entry points, and delete the repeated execution of line 299 on the shard-to-time-split path.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real architectural concern in the diff. Looking at the code: shardQuerySplitting.ts:52 applies `datasource.applyTemplateVariables()` to queries, and querySplitting.ts:299 also applies the same transformation. The finding claims that when shard splitting delegates to time splitting via runSplitQuery, the template variables would be applied twice. However, examining the diff more carefully: runShardSplitQuery processes queries and passes them to splitQueriesByStreamShard, which eventually may call runSplitQuery. The concern about duplicate processing is valid - both entry points now normalize queries, so if one calls the other, normalization happens twice. This is a legitimate efficiency/architecture concern introduced by the diff, though not a correctness bug since applying template variables twice should be idempotent. It's an important non-bug issue about code structure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/plugins/datasource/loki/querySplitting.ts:298 — P3, confidence 100: the verbatim sequence `.filter((query) => query.expr)` followed by `.map((query) => datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters))` (also `public/app/plugins/datasource/loki/shardQuerySplitting.ts:50-52`) filters the raw expression before interpolation, so when a nonempty variable-only expression such as `$selector` resolves to `''` it survives selection and an empty query is sent to Loki instead of being omitted, producing a backend parse error and failing the panel, while the added tests cover only nonempty substitutions and therefore miss this acceptance case.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the diff changes the order of operations: filtering on `query.expr` now happens BEFORE `applyTemplateVariables` is called. This means if a query has `expr: '$selector'` (truthy, non-empty string), it passes the filter. But if `$selector` resolves to an empty string `''`, the query will still be sent to Loki because the filter already passed. Previously with `interpolateVariablesInQueries`, the interpolation happened first, then filtering would catch empty results. The diff shows this exact pattern in both querySplitting.ts (lines 296-299) and shardQuerySplitting.ts (lines 49-52). The tests added only cover cases where variables resolve to non-empty values ('5m'), not the edge case where a variable resolves to empty string.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/plugins/datasource/loki/querySplitting.ts:298 — severity P3, confidence 100: the verbatim ordering `.filter((query) => query.expr)` before `.map((query) => datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters))` (repeated at `public/app/plugins/datasource/loki/shardQuerySplitting.ts:50-52`) fails when a nonempty variable-only expression resolves to `''`, because the raw target passes the filter and the split pipeline sends an empty expression instead of omitting it; the strongest counterargument is that selector variables are normally nonempty, but custom and scoped variables accept empty values, so the extra invalid request remains reachable.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the diff changes the order of operations: filtering for non-empty `query.expr` happens BEFORE template variable interpolation via `applyTemplateVariables`. If a query has `expr: '$myVar'` where `$myVar` is a variable that resolves to an empty string, the filter `query.expr` would pass (since '$myVar' is truthy), but after interpolation the expression becomes empty. This would result in sending an invalid empty expression to the query pipeline. The diff at lines 296-299 in querySplitting.ts and lines 49-52 in shardQuerySplitting.ts both show this pattern where filtering occurs before the map that applies template variables.
